customManagers.description: CI installs npm CLIs from `run:` steps rather than a manifest, so Renovate's npm manager never saw them and the 24h quarantine did not apply (Issue #3642). Match the exact `pkg@1.2.3` pins in .github/workflows/*.yml so those bumps go through `minimumReleaseAge` like every other ecosystem.

`gem install bundler-audit` runs outside the Gemfile tree, so Renovate's bundler manager never saw it (Issue #3642). Match the exact `-v 1.2.3` pin in .github/workflows/*.yml so it is quarantined and kept current.

The Deno the workflows install comes from `.deno-version` — one source of truth tied to the container image's Deno by test (Issue #4403). Track denoland/deno releases so the pin is bumped under minimumReleaseAge instead of going stale.
The Node the workflows install comes from `.node-version` — tied to the container image's NODE_VERSION by test (Issue #4403).

packageRules.description: Deno (JSR / deno.land/x) dependencies are intentionally governed by native Deno tooling — deno.json `minimumDependencyAge` — not Renovate. Disable Renovate's deno manager so the two mechanisms do not overlap or conflict for Deno (Issue #2536; native window added in #2539). The 24h window and the stSoftwareAU/* exemption below still apply to the ecosystems Renovate owns (e.g. GitHub Actions).

Internal stSoftwareAU/* packages bypass the supply-chain quarantine — they are first-party code and ship with no embargo (Issue #2124). This is a standing first-party-code exemption, NOT the emergency override for an actively-exploited third-party CVE — for that, see docs/security-advisory-triage.md#emergency-dependency-override (Issue #2509).
